title: SIU identifies man killed after confrontation that began when he reportedly refused to wear mask at grocery store
article: Ontario's police watchdog has identified the 73-year-old man killed last month by police officers northeast of Haliburton , after he allegedly assaulted a Minden grocery store employee over a mask dispute.
On Thursday, the Special Investigations Unit identified the man as Leslie Hegedus .
The SIU says officers were called around 9:25 a.m. on July 15 to a grocery store for an assault report.

In an interview with the Star last month, OPP Sgt. Jason Folz said the worker was cleaning carts outside the store and attempted to give the man a free mask, which all customers are required to wear to enter, when he was assaulted.
The man then left, driving "dangerously" through the parking lot, Folz said.
Outside of the man's residence about a 30-minute drive away, the SIU said there was an "interaction" and two officers shot him.
He was transported to hospital where he was pronounced dead shortly before noon, the SIU said at the time.
The SIU said Thursday that five civilian witnesses and four witness officers were interviewed. Another officer was designated as a witness officer, but investigators only requested the notes.
Both officers who were designated as subject officers consented to interviews and submitted their notes.
The SIU is an arm's-length agency that investigates reports involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.

The SIU is urging anyone who may have information about this investigation to contact the lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529. The SIU is also urging anyone who may have any video evidence related to this incident to upload that video through the agency's website.
Raneem Alozzi is a breaking news reporter, working out of the Star's radio room in Toronto. Follow her on Twitter: @r_alozzi With files from Ted Fraser
